title: Trace a release through evidence and drift response
description: Switch incidents to see how the platform keeps new releases bounded, records evidence, and restores a compatible state without turning monitoring into the serving path.

nodes.label: Versioned data
nodes.detail: Publishes validated, time-bounded data snapshots and source-schema changes for feature and training jobs.

nodes.label: Feature contract
nodes.detail: Defines point-in-time transformations, freshness rules, defaults, and online/offline compatibility for every feature version.

nodes.label: Training and eval
nodes.detail: Produces a candidate artifact and slice-level offline evidence from reproducible data, code, and feature inputs.

nodes.label: Model registry
nodes.detail: Binds the artifact, owners, evaluation, approvals, serving contract, and rollback target to one governed release record.

nodes.label: Canary serving
nodes.detail: Routes a bounded cohort to the approved candidate with compatible features, deadlines, policy, and a retained prior release.

nodes.label: Versioned monitoring
nodes.detail: Joins exposures and predictions to outcome, drift, freshness, fairness, latency, and fallback signals by release and cohort.

nodes.label: Rollout controller
nodes.detail: Pauses promotion, shifts cohorts, and restores the previously approved compatible release when release policy fails.

scenarios.label: Healthy canary
scenarios.summary: The candidate has compatible inputs and approval evidence. A representative cohort receives it while outcomes and service signals are recorded asynchronously.
scenarios.result: The controller can promote only after online guardrails and the required evidence window remain healthy; telemetry never delays a prediction.

scenarios.label: Feature drift
scenarios.summary: A production feature distribution or freshness signal moves outside the release contract even though the request path still returns successful responses.
scenarios.result: The controller freezes promotion and restores the prior compatible release or declared fallback while owners investigate the feature change.

scenarios.label: Outcome regression
scenarios.summary: Delayed labels show that the candidate harms a critical slice despite healthy infrastructure and acceptable aggregate traffic metrics.
scenarios.result: The release policy treats the slice breach as a rollback trigger. The candidate evidence remains available for diagnosis rather than being silently overwritten.

scenarios.label: Monitoring backlog
scenarios.summary: The monitoring pipeline cannot evaluate new evidence promptly. Serving remains available, but the platform has lost the proof needed for additional promotion.
scenarios.result: Keep the canary bounded or restore the prior release. Do not promote on missing evidence merely because the service remains fast.

scenarios.label: Registry unavailable
scenarios.summary: The registry is unavailable during a release request. The platform must not create an untraceable deployment or discard the version already serving.
scenarios.result: Existing approved traffic can continue, but new promotion stops. The controller can still restore the retained compatible release through its pre-established rollout state.
